ap_chemistry-f01.title: Lewis structure, geometry and boiling points

stimulus.description: Consider the molecule $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ and the two compounds $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH}$ (46.1 g/mol, normal boiling point 351 K) and $\mathrm{CH_{3}OCH_{3}}$ (46.1 g/mol, normal boiling point 248 K).

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw a Lewis electron-dot diagram of $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ that shows all of its valence electrons.
parts.model_answer: H2O has 8 valence electrons in total. A correct diagram shows two O–H single bonds and 2 lone pairs on O.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws a Lewis diagram that accounts for all 8 valence electrons: two O–H single bonds and 2 lone pairs on O
common_errors: omits the lone pairs on the central atom

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Use your diagram to identify the molecular geometry of $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ and the approximate bond angle.
parts.model_answer: bent; bond angle slightly less than 109.5° (about 104.5°) (four electron domains (two bonding pairs and two lone pairs) are arranged tetrahedrally and the lone pairs make the molecule bent).

rubric_rows.criterion: States bent geometry and a bond angle of slightly less than 109.5° (about 104.5°)
common_errors: reports the electron-domain geometry instead of the molecular geometry

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Is the $\mathrm{H_{2}O}$ molecule polar or nonpolar? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: Polar: the bond dipoles do not cancel because the shape is not symmetric.

rubric_rows.criterion: States polar and links it to a shape in which the bond dipoles do not cancel
common_errors: decides by the polarity of the bonds alone

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The data in the stimulus show that $\mathrm{C_{2}H_{5}OH}$ has a higher boiling point than $\mathrm{CH_{3}OCH_{3}}$ even though it has a similar molar mass. Explain this difference in terms of intermolecular forces.
parts.model_answer: C2H5OH molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another, which are stronger than the attractions between CH3OCH3 molecules, so more energy is needed to separate the molecules of C2H5OH.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies hydrogen bonding between C2H5OH molecules (a hydrogen atom bonded to N, O or F) as stronger than the attractions between CH3OCH3 molecules, which raises the boiling point
common_errors: says covalent bonds within the molecules break when the liquid boils

ap_chemistry-f02.title: Equilibrium expression, Q versus K and disturbances

stimulus.description: At a certain temperature the equilibrium $\mathrm{A}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\,\mathrm{B}(g)$ has $K_c=0.5$ and is endothermic. A cylinder with a movable piston initially contains $[\mathrm{A}]=0.5\text{ M}$ and $[\mathrm{B}]=0.3\text{ M}$ at this temperature.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Write the equilibrium-constant expression, $K_c$, for the reaction.
parts.model_answer: $K_c=[\mathrm{B}]^2/[\mathrm{A}]$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes $[\mathrm{B}]^2/[\mathrm{A}]$ (products over reactant, with the coefficient as an exponent)
common_errors: omits the exponent 2

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the reaction quotient, $Q$, for the initial mixture and determine the direction in which the reaction proceeds.
parts.model_answer: $Q=0.3^2/0.5=0.18$, which is less than $K_c=0.5$, so the reaction proceeds toward the products.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $Q\approx 0.18$ and states the direction as forward by comparing Q with K
common_errors: reverses the comparison of Q and K

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: After the system reaches equilibrium, the piston is moved so that the volume of the cylinder is doubled at constant temperature. Predict the direction of the shift and justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The system shifts toward the products: the expansion lowers the concentrations, $Q$ becomes less than $K_c$, and the side with more moles of gas (two moles of B instead of one of A) is favored at lower pressure.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the shift toward the products and justifies it with either Q becoming less than K after the expansion or the favored side having more moles of gas
alt_solutions: Q becomes less than K after the expansion
the side with more moles of gas is favored at lower pressure
common_errors: says K changes with volume

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The temperature is then increased. Does the value of $K_c$ increase or decrease? Justify your answer using the sign of the enthalpy change.
parts.model_answer: $K_c$ increases: for an endothermic reaction heat acts as a reactant, so raising the temperature favors the products.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that $K_c$ increases and justifies it with the enthalpy change: heat acts as a reactant in an endothermic reaction, so added heat favors the products
alt_solutions: the equilibrium shifts toward the products when heat is added
common_errors: says K does not depend on temperature
